propositions: A configured provider is silently discarded when a model id contains a colon (e.g. canonical versioned Bedrock ids like `us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0`)
The `_resolve_target` function incorrectly tests `if ":" in model` to detect already-qualified strings, misinterpreting colons within version suffixes as provider separators
Downstream, unqualified model strings are parsed on the first colon, extracting a fragment of the model id (e.g. `us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1`) and reporting it as an unknown provider
An explicitly configured provider must be checked before scanning the model string, so punctuation in a model id cannot override or discard it
The qualified/unqualified decision must be centralized in one shared function to prevent independent implementations from drifting and introducing the same bug separately
A conflicting configured-provider and inline-qualifier pair must raise an error rather than silently choosing a winner, as either choice discards an explicit instruction
